doc_verification.detail: Reachability: my WebFetch of https://api.qdrant.tech/v-1-18-x/api-reference/distributed/collection-cluster-info was blocked by network policy (domain_blocked -> PARTIAL, not FAIL); offset by two indirect records: (a) the contract's endpoint_registry carries a build-time verified doc_quote for this exact URL ('Returns 200 with CollectionClusterInfo; 404 for an unknown collection.', verified_at 2026-09-02T12:34:08Z), and (b) the target clone bundles the identical versioned spec at docs/redoc/v1.18.x/openapi.json, which is the source of the versioned doc site. Version: v-1-18.x == 1.18.x matches target v1.18.0 (PASS). Content consistency FAIL on the load-bearing part: the contract assertion demands unconditional containment of resharding_operations, but the CollectionClusterInfo schema in the v1.18.x OpenAPI lists required=[local_shards, peer_id, remote_shards, shard_count, shard_transfers] and marks resharding_operations as "nullable": true, NOT required (openapi.json lines 12168-12220) — the doc does not promise the field's presence; the mine's own raw_knowledge notation also asterisked only peer_id*/shard_count* as required (raw_knowledge.json:3246). The other five fields' containment is doc-grounded and was observed present. Endpoint precision PASS: registry maps cluster+collection+info to GET /collections/{collection_name}/cluster (raw_knowledge.json:3233); the script polls exactly this route via runtime alias collection_cluster.

http_semantics.note: Primary observation is a response-shape omission on HTTP 200s, not a request-side client error being swallowed; no illegal-parameter acceptance is involved.

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: response contains peer_id, shard_count (minimum 0), local_shards, remote_shards, shard_transfers, resharding_operations
contract_grounding.note: constraint_id recovered from the script header (state_cluster_collection_info_004.py line 6 'constraint_ids: qdrant_type_cluster_collection_info_001'); the candidates.jsonl dispatch entry had an empty constraint_id field. api_violates_assertion=true is the LITERAL reading: observed 200s lack resharding_operations while the contract text says 'response contains ... resharding_operations'. However the doc-grounded reading is false: the cited v1.18.x OpenAPI marks the field nullable and NOT required, so the violation is against the contract's over-strong flattening of the schema, not against the published documentation; source forensics further shows the omission is an explicit by-design serde skip. All five doc-required fields were present in every observed response.

doc: v1.18.x OpenAPI CollectionClusterInfo requires only [local_shards, peer_id, remote_shards, shard_count, shard_transfers]; resharding_operations is nullable:true and not required — the doc does NOT support unconditional containment of the one field whose absence triggered the DEFECT

log: DEFECT line reports exactly 2x '200 missing [resharding_operations]' (the >=2 reproduction rule met); the same log's post-settle [info face] read also lacks the field and [reconcile] shows count_face=200 == local_sum=200 == expected — the concurrency/Type4-state attribution is contradicted by the log's own steady-state evidence
chain_trace.break_detail: The contract->doc link is broken for the decisive field: the assertion's unconditional containment of resharding_operations is stronger than the cited documentation (nullable, not in required). Secondary weakness at the log link: the DEFECT text attributes the omission to 'writes' and types it Type4_StateLogicViolation, but the same log and four sibling logs show the field is omitted unconditionally (idle, post-insert, post-delete, during-churn), i.e., a static serialization policy rather than a concurrency state violation; the actual concurrency oracle (count reconciliation, zero 5xx) came out clean.

files_examined: docs/redoc/v1.18.x/openapi.json (12168-12220: CollectionClusterInfo schema served by the versioned doc site)
source_grounding.call_chain_traced: actix route GET /collections/{collection_name}/cluster (src/actix/api/collections_api.rs:198 get_cluster_info) -> do_get_collection_cluster -> Collection::cluster_info (lib/collection/src/collection/collection_ops.rs:434-468) -> shards_holder.get_resharding_operations_info() (lib/collection/src/shards/shard_holder/mod.rs:534) which returns None whenever self.resharding_state.read() is None (no active resharding — always the case in this test) -> serde serialization drops the key via #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] (types.rs:341) -> REST JSON omits resharding_operations unconditionally in the absence of resharding. gRPC face: From<CollectionClusterInfo> for grpc CollectionClusterInfoResponse (conversions.rs:1537-1564) flattens the Option into an always-materialized empty repeated field.
source_grounding.note: by_design evidence is explicit, not inferred: the maintainer comment '// TODO(resharding): remove this skip when releasing resharding' sits directly on the skip attribute, qdrant's own consensus-test utils defensively handle the field's absence (utils.py:582,588), and the published v1.18.x OpenAPI itself marks the field nullable/not-required — so behavior, source intent, and the published schema are mutually consistent; the only artifact claiming unconditional presence is the contract's flattened assertion text.

mundane_explanation.surviving: by_design: resharding_operations is conditionally omitted via an explicitly commented serde skip (Option::is_none) whenever no resharding operation is active; the published OpenAPI marks the field nullable/not-required, so the surviving mismatch is contract-assertion-vs-doc/source, not API-vs-doc
